candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication actions/indications and medication-related client education
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — acarbose / alpha-glucosidase inhibitor mechanism
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that acarbose lowers postprandial glucose by delaying carbohydrate digestion and glucose absorption through alpha-amylase/intestinal alpha-glucosidase inhibition rather than by stimulating insulin secretion.

options.A: It competitively inhibits intestinal alpha-glucosidases and pancreatic alpha-amylase, delaying carbohydrate digestion and glucose absorption and reducing postprandial hyperglycemia
options.B: It directly stimulates pancreatic beta cells to release more insulin
options.C: It blocks renal glucose reabsorption so more glucose is excreted in the urine
options.D: It inhibits DPP-4, prolonging endogenous incretin hormone activity

candidate.rationale: Current acarbose labeling states that the drug competitively and reversibly inhibits pancreatic alpha-amylase and membrane-bound intestinal alpha-glucoside hydrolases. This delays carbohydrate digestion and glucose absorption and lowers the postprandial rise in glucose. Acarbose does not enhance insulin secretion. Renal glucose-reabsorption blockade describes SGLT2 inhibitors, while DPP-4 inhibition describes agents such as sitagliptin. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Acarbose delays carbohydrate digestion and glucose absorption and lowers postprandial hyperglycemia through pancreatic alpha-amylase and intestinal alpha-glucosidase inhibition.
candidate.source_locator: Clinical Pharmacology > Mechanism of Action: acarbose does not enhance insulin secretion; competitive reversible inhibition of pancreatic alpha-amylase and membrane-bound intestinal alpha-glucoside hydrolases delays glucose absorption and lowers postprandial hyperglycemia

candidate.stem: A client with type 2 diabetes is prescribed acarbose. Which explanation of its action is most accurate?
